newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria cracks down on car crime, tax evasion.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria cracks down on car crime, tax evasion.

text.p: Bulgarian police have checked 14,600 luxury cars and their owners in a crackdown codenamed Operation Mosquito on car theft and tax evasion, the interior ministry said on Wednesday.
The countrywide operation began last Thursday.

"The main thing we achieved was a clear idea about the attitude to tax of all these rich people, because not a single one of the owners presented us with a declaration that he paid tax on the income with which he bought the car," Ministry Chief Secretary Bozhdar Popov told reporters.
"We found some people did not know that they had to pay income tax at all."
The interim government which took office last month has vowed to get tough on the crime and corruption which have flourished in the seven years since the end of one-party rule.
Drivers in Sofia were escorted to a barracks on the outskirts of the capital where the checks were carried out.
Popov said the cars inspected had included the Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Audi and Opel marques and a variety of luxury four-wheel drive vehicles.

He said they had found evidence of 52 criminal cases and had detained 19 people, adding that 100 cars had had the serial number on their engine altered, and the owners of 24 of those 100 had been identified so far.

Police say Bulgarian groups working with gangs in Western Europe alter the appearance of vehicles and forge their documents, ready for local sale or re-export to neighbouring Balkan countries and former Soviet republics.
The head of the National Police Directorate said last week that Bulgaria urgently needed to update its legislation in order to combat rising street and organised crime.

The crackdown on ill-gotten wealth has been generally welcomed by the public, though some critics dismiss it as a publicity stunt, saying the same information could be found in police and finance ministry records.
Others say it will not affect the biggest criminals whose money is outside Bulgaria, beyond the reach of the authorities.
Popov said the next phase of Operation Mosquito would be a check on the owners of expensive villas. "We will investigate everyone showing a luxury lifestyle," he said.
